rows.text: Two things are happening at once. Saruman turns every noncreature spell you cast into +1/+1 counters on a single Army equal to that spell's mana value — so the interaction you were holding up anyway assembles a lethal creature for free. And the spell list itself is pointed squarely at the decks Grixis usually loses to: white prison and green ramp. Gloom, Perish, Dystopia, Hibernation and Filter Out are not filler, they are the reason the deck exists.

rows.name: Saruman, the White Hand
rows.text: every noncreature spell amasses Orcs equal to its mana value, and your Orcs and Goblins have ward {2}. A Cyclonic Rift is seven counters. A Mana Drain is two. The Army is your clock and your blocker and it never needed a card slot of its own.

rows.name: Orcish Siegemaster
rows.text: your Orcs and Goblins gain trample, and it attacks for the greatest power on your board. It is what stops the Army being chump-blocked forever.

rows.name: Lazotep Plating
rows.text: amass one AND hexproof for you and everything you control. It is a counterspell for removal, a fog for a targeted wrath, and a Saruman trigger.

rows.name: Slip Out the Back
rows.text: one mana to phase the Army out of a wrath, plus a counter.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Ovika, Enigma Goliath
rows.text: X hasty Goblins for every noncreature spell, where X is its mana value. Alongside Saruman, one big spell is a board and a lethal Army in the same breath — and the Goblins get ward from Saruman and trample from Orcish Siegemaster.

rows.name: Sedgemoor Witch
rows.text: a Pest for every instant and sorcery, with menace and ward on the body.

rows.name: Archmage Emeritus
rows.text: a card for every instant and sorcery you cast or copy.

rows.name: Guttersnipe
rows.text: two damage to each opponent per instant and sorcery.

rows.name: Birgi, God of Storytelling
rows.text: red mana on every spell you cast, which is how the big turns get bigger. The back face turns dead cards into two impulse draws.

rows.name: Gloom
rows.text: white spells cost {3} more, and activated abilities of white enchantments cost {3} more. Against a prison or Voltron deck this is close to a lock, and the second clause specifically answers the enchantments Grixis cannot destroy.

rows.name: Dystopia
rows.text: every player sacrifices a green or white permanent every upkeep. You have none, so it is entirely one-sided, and the cumulative upkeep is paid in life.

rows.name: Deathmark
rows.text: one mana for a green or white creature.

rows.name: Debt to the Kami
rows.text: they exile a creature OR an enchantment of their choice. Edicts are how Grixis answers a hexproof enchantment.

rows.name: Pharika's Libation
rows.text: the same, at instant speed, as a sacrifice.

rows.name: Extract the Truth
rows.text: strips a creature, enchantment or planeswalker from their hand, or forces an enchantment sacrifice.

rows.name: Perish
rows.text: destroys every green creature on the board. Against an elf or ramp deck it is a one-sided wrath for three mana.

rows.name: Hibernation
rows.text: returns every green PERMANENT to hand — creatures, enchantments, mana auras and all. It undoes an entire green deck's turn.

rows.name: Ashiok, Dream Render
rows.text: opponents cannot search their libraries at all. Fetchlands, tutors, Cultivate and every green ramp spell stop working.

rows.name: Opposition Agent
rows.text: flash him in and you control their search. Everything they find is yours.

rows.name: Filter Out
rows.text: returns ALL noncreature, nonland permanents to their owners' hands. Every prison enchantment, every mana rock, every Equipment at the table, gone at instant speed — and it is a four-counter Saruman trigger on top.

rows.name: Rushing River
rows.text: bounce one permanent, or two if you kick it. Instant speed answers to a lock piece.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, the same effect aimed only at them, and it amasses seven.

rows.name: Brotherhood's End
rows.text: three damage to every creature and planeswalker, or every cheap artifact destroyed. Pick whichever half the table is built on.

rows.name: Imprisoned in the Moon
rows.text: turns a commander, a land or a planeswalker into a colourless land they cannot recast.

rows.name: Reality Shift
rows.text: exile a creature and leave them a face-down 2/2.

rows.name: Feed the Swarm
rows.text: the rare black spell that kills an enchantment outright.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the answer to anything at all, once.

rows.name: Counterspell
rows.text: two counters and the answer.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: two counters, and the mana casts the next spell.

rows.name: Mana Sculpt
rows.text: three counters, and with a Wizard out — which is nearly always — it refunds their mana to you.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: free on their turn.

rows.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
rows.text: one mana for anything noncreature.

rows.name: Muddle the Mixture
rows.text: a counterspell, or transmute for any three-drop — Sedgemoor Witch, Ovika's setup, or Dimir Machinations.

rows.name: Baral, Chief of Compliance
rows.text: cheaper spells, and a loot every time you counter something.

rows.name: Flame of Anor
rows.text: with a Wizard out, take two of three modes. Draw two and kill a creature, usually.

rows.name: Dark Ritual
rows.text: three black on turn one.

rows.name: Seething Song
rows.text: five red for three.

rows.name: Rite of Flame
rows.text: cheap acceleration that is also a Saruman trigger.

rows.name: Goblin Electromancer
rows.text: instants and sorceries cost one less.

rows.name: Nightscape Familiar
rows.text: the same for blue and red, on a regenerating body.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card.

rows.name: Grim Tutor
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Merchant Scroll
rows.text: any blue instant, which usually means a counterspell or Filter Out.

rows.name: Dimir Machinations
rows.text: transmute for a three-drop, or strip their top three cards.

rows.name: Ringsight
rows.text: any card sharing a colour with a legend you control.

rows.name: Impulse
rows.text: dig four at instant speed.

rows.name: Pieces of the Puzzle
rows.text: two instants or sorceries from the top five.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep interaction and mana, not threats. The Army IS the threat, and it only exists because you cast spells — a hand of counterspells and removal is a hand of Saruman triggers.

Read the table before you keep the hosers. Gloom, Perish, Dystopia and Hibernation are dead cards against a mono-black or artifact table and game-winning against a green or white one. Against the wrong pod they are your worst four cards, so spend them as Saruman fodder rather than holding them.

rows.name: Saruman, the White Hand
rows.text: four mana, and every turn he is out is counters you are not getting. He is a 2/5 that blocks well, so he is safer to deploy early than most commanders of his cost.

rows.name: Ovika, Enigma Goliath
rows.text: hold her until you have a big spell to follow with. Landing her and immediately overloading Cyclonic Rift is seven Goblins with haste, seven counters on the Army, and usually the game.
